title: E37 could not resolve the tool's FPS cost because the noise lives BETWEEN rig loads: two off_baseline replicates at effectively identical load (53.5 vs 53.9 units) differed by 16.5%, which swamps any plausible cost of a few Lua jobs. More replicates would not fix that; a different design does. E38 toggles the tool's JOBS on and off in alternating 8,000-tick blocks INSIDE a single replicate, so on-samples and off-samples share one rig load, one save, one thermal state and one population trajectory, and the between-load variance differences away. The scheduler is toggled directly through repeat-util rather than through disableSched(), because disableSched() also runs CAVERN.restoreAll() and writes config to disk - a per-toggle cost that would be charged to whichever phase followed it. The measured frame rate belongs to the interval just ended, so each receipt records the state in force DURING that interval, not the state it is about to switch to. A sham arm runs the identical block bookkeeping while never touching the scheduler: it measures what the method itself appears to find when there is nothing to find.
fork: Does the tool's recurring job cost survive a paired within-replicate comparison, and is the sham arm's apparent difference small enough for the method to be trusted.

predictions.expects: the paired on-minus-off difference is within the sham arm's apparent difference, 2 of 2 - the jobs are free at this fort's scale

predictions.model: a small recurring cost that pairing can see
predictions.expects: on-samples run consistently below off-samples within each replicate, same sign in both, and clearly beyond the sham arm's spread

predictions.model: the method cannot see it either
predictions.expects: the sham arm shows an apparent difference as large as the real arm's - within-replicate noise is itself too big, and FPS on this rig is not measurable at this effect size by any 2-replicate design

kill_criterion: a within-replicate paired difference consistent in sign across both replicates AND larger than the sham arm's apparent difference; a real difference smaller than the sham's is not a cost
culling: drop a replicate on any changed save
discard the first sample of every block: calculated_fps is a rolling average and has not settled after a toggle
a replicate whose receipts never alternate `during=` is a trigger failure - the toggle did not fire
a replicate running at the fps cap is vacuous

pre: local sw=reqscript('seasonal-wildlife'); local cfg=sw.loadConfig(); if not cfg.initialized then sw.captureDefault(cfg) end; cfg.layers.land=true; cfg.layers.water=true; cfg.layers.cavern=true; local pool=sw.buildPool(cfg); local n=0; for _,e in ipairs(pool) do if e.inEmbark and sw.defaultAllow(e) then cfg.allow[e.key]=true; n=n+1 end end; local a=sw.assignFromMatrix(cfg,pool); cfg.groups.enabled=true; cfg.groups.coupling=true; cfg.groups.pack=4; cfg.groups.cohesion=true; cfg.ecology.enabled=true; cfg.water.enabled=true; cfg.quota.cavern=0; cfg.enabled=true; sw.saveConfig(cfg); sw.applyLive(cfg, df.global.cur_season); sw.saveConfig(cfg); sw.enableSched(); print(('e38: roster applied - %d allowed, %d assigned; jobs start ON'):format(n,a))

pre: local sw=reqscript('seasonal-wildlife'); local cfg=sw.loadConfig(); if not cfg.initialized then sw.captureDefault(cfg) end; cfg.enabled=false; cfg.groups.enabled=false; cfg.ecology.enabled=false; cfg.water.enabled=false; sw.saveConfig(cfg); sw.disableSched(); print('e38: SHAM - tool off throughout; block bookkeeping runs but never toggles')
